catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue class fits the pinned stop. cap.motion.stop.v1 declares an optional deceleration profile and reports stopped_at/stopped_position, while ADAM/Navigation only command targetVelocity=0 (scripts/navigation.py:23-34 and :160-169) and expose no wheel-speed readback or deceleration profile. The input-free extension preserves that native call and is the safe_state.achieved_by action.

notes:
PASS on the fake backend only; evidence is contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level. Model-authored and unreviewed: driver.lock.json authored_by is the deepseek-v4.1-flash:1017 model with run_id ros-wave-c-122 and reviewed_by stays null. No human reviewed or tested anything; no hardware was attached; no hardware run is claimed. No ROS graph, rosbridge connection, PyBullet process or upstream import/run was used, and the clone was left unmodified. The gate ran G1-G9, all passed with zero findings and zero warnings.

DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: task.json says family ros, helper RosDriver. The pinned runtime that owns the simulation and the base control is the Python class scripts.adam:ADAM (scripts/adam.py:20-70): ADAM.step calls p.stepSimulation() and then sleeps for self.t (scripts/adam.py:173-193), and Navigation.send_velocity converts a linear/angular velocity into the two wheel targets (scripts/navigation.py:200-217). The ROS layer is the simulator's bridge to a real ADAM robot: ROSConnection creates a node, subscribes to /robot/left_arm/joint_states and /robot/right_arm/joint_states, publishes the two /robot/<arm>/scaled_pos_traj_controller/command JointTrajectory topics and /robot/move_base/cmd_vel, and offers no pause, stop or reset service (scripts/ros_connection.py:14-25, :40-53, :240-260). A configuration-only RosDriver cannot start the PyBullet process, and declaring those real-robot publications as the control path would misdescribe the simulator, so this package uses a direct Driver over ADAM.

WHAT IT SERVES: cap.motion.mobile_base.v1 drive takes {linear_velocity, angular_velocity, duration_s}, applies the upstream Navigation.send_velocity clamp, calls ADAM.step once per self.t tick, then commands both wheel targets to zero. Its distance_m/heading_rad are dead-reckoned from the applied velocities, not measured by an upstream odometry getter. x-cap.mobile-robots-group-uc3m.zero_wheels.v1 is input-free, calls Navigation.move_wheels(0.0, 0.0) and is the safe_state.achieved_by action; the @estop calls the same native method. Reads are camera_angle (Sensors.get_camera_angle) and the two six-joint arm arrays (ArmsKinematics.get_arm_joint_angles).

SAFETY AND LIMITS: risk R2 because the upstream is a simulated mobile base (MHS/spec/04-safety.md); the card floor is R0. The velocity and duration inputs have no sourced device bound: the only upstream velocity clamp is Navigation.linear_speed/angular_speed, configurable constructor defaults (scripts/navigation.py:14-15, applied at :208-209), and ADAM.step is a caller-driven loop (scripts/adam.py:173-193). They are Limit.operator_required and the runtime refuses the drive until a site overlay supplies them; site-limits.example.json is an illustrative overlay, not a device limit. The stop is a zero wheel-velocity target plus the driver ceasing to call ADAM.step; the upstream exposes no wheel-velocity or base-odometry getter, so stopped=True records that the command was applied, not measured quiescence. No physical e-stop is claimed or cited; the runtime latch is the local barrier.

NOT COVERED: arm and hand motion, gripper commands, camera RGB-D images, lidar rays, /robot topics and hand services, any live or sim PyBullet backend, reset, snapshot/restore and hardware. The fake is a pure-Python kinematic stand-in, not a recording: it runs no PyBullet, physics, contacts, wheel friction, sensors or GUI, and its start pose, camera angle and arm angles are placeholders. The upstream simulator needs pybullet and a PyBullet GUI client (scripts/adam.py:51), ROS 1 Noetic and Python 3.8 (Readme.md:39); it was neither installed nor run, and a separately reviewed backend would be required before a deployment could rely on it. Only the fake backend factory exists (.fake:FakeAdam); no native.py is present. The camera angle is exposed as a scalar observation only; the RGB-D arrays are outside this scope. test_driver.py keeps check_driver and adds five repository cases covering the reads, the unfilled operator-required refusal, the example-overlay drive, the stop action and the e-stop latch.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Checked the direct-Driver deviation (ADAMSim is a PyBullet Python simulator; its ROS layer is a bridge to the real ADAM robot), all 17 facts, the operator_required velocity and duration limits, the fake against Navigation and ADAM, and the stop path. Defects: the drive action zeroed the wheel targets only on cancellation, so a failing ADAM.step left them at the commanded velocity (a reviewer probe on the author's copy left 0.2 m/s and 0.1 rad/s), and with use_ros every step fails at the pin because ROSConnection.sleep reads self.adam.useRealTimeSimulation, which ADAM never assigns (it stores use_realtime); facts.md said the simulation no longer advances once the driver stops stepping, which is false in PyBullet real-time mode (use_realtime, the ADAM default); the camera fact omitted the -45 offset of get_camera_angle; the Navigation fact called hard-coded attributes 'configurable constructor defaults, not device limits'; and the default fixed base (no Navigation), the stdout prints, the robot_info JSON write and ROSConnection's real-robot mirroring and unbounded wait_for_service were undisclosed. Reviewer changed driver.py (try/finally zeroing on every exit, safe_state for both PyBullet modes, camera and Navigation facts corrected, eight source facts, three fidelity gaps, docstring and descriptions), test_driver.py (a failing-step case) and facts.md, and regenerated reference.json, REFERENCE.md and check-report.json; the gate and collect.py --strict pass and the digest is unchanged. The author's notes calling the Navigation clamps configurable constructor defaults are superseded. The card needs the owner's publication decision (publish_review required; licence not stated (NOASSERTION)); the package may not be published or merged into a published tree before it. For the human reviewer: Fake-only contract: no live backend is declared. A live backend must construct ADAM(use_fixed_base=False, use_ros=False): with the defaults there is no Navigation, and with use_ros every ADAM.step raises AttributeError at the pin. Constructing ADAM opens a PyBullet GUI, prints to stdout (which would corrupt a stdio MHS server), may write the robot_info JSON into the clone, and with use_ros initialises a ROS node that mirrors the real robot's arms at 120 Hz, blocks without a timeout on the real hands' services and holds publishers to the real UR arm controllers and the base's /robot/move_base/cmd_vel (this driver never calls them). The stop is a zero wheel-velocity target (force 100), not measured rest; in real-time mode the world keeps running.
